subject: hydra
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: five-headed hydra.
Style: God of War.
reasoning:
I'm planning a full Hydra model in a God of War style: a heavy quadruped body with five necks and a tail, dark scarred scales, bone spikes, glowing runes, and remnants of chains and armor, keeping effects grim and ember-lit while sticking to the available imports.

Now I'm laying out the skeleton -- placing hip/pelvis joints, building a spine chain of named joints along catmull points for the torso, and sweeping that chain into a tapered body shape with elliptical radii that shift toward the belly.

Still working out the sweep geometry...

For the tail, I'm building a separate chain of five joints extending backward and downward from the pelvis, tapering with decreasing radii for a whip-like shape. Now I'm planning the five necks branching from the chest area, fanning out across lateral offset positions and considering whether to use surface-sprouting or simple chains rooted at points on the body.

Working out the neck curves and head placements...

Still defining neck joints...

Still defining head shapes...

Adding more facial features...

Now sizing each head individually with a scale multiplier, giving the central head more prominence. Then I'm working out leg placement — front legs off the chest, hind legs off the pelvis — figuring out joint positions and segment lengths to keep the stance proportional.

For the front elbow I'll bend backward instead, then build the foot box at the ankle tip with claws as three forward spikes radiating from the toe area, checking that the foot bottom sits right at y=0 as the ground plane while the body stays well above it.

Now I'm defining the pelvis joint and the spine chain that sweeps up from hips to shoulders, shaping the body radius so it tapers naturally with a sine curve and considering adding rib-like armor sectors along the torso instead of a softer belly patch.

I'm thinking of embedding a broken Norse axe into the creature's flank as a decorative touch, like a Leviathan axe with glowing blue frost runes stuck in the body near the side, giving it that God of War weapon-embedded aesthetic.

Now I'm adding glowing ember cracks scattered across the body using thin flat boxes positioned as scorched lava-like scars, around 14 of them with randomized orientation, plus scales made from small flattened dark-green plates scattered across the surface for texture.

I'm settling on a color palette covering skin tones, bone, ember glow, eyes, rust, steel, frost, and leather, then considering adding God of War-style iron shackles with chains on one of the necks for extra detail.

Writing collar and chain code...

Still writing head loft stations...

Still placing head features...

Scattering scale boxes across the neck surface, then shifting to shoulder bulk spheres bound to chest/spine bones and pelvis for hips, with thigh sweeps tapering from hip radius. Now I'm setting up the leg-building function that takes root, foot, segment lengths, bend, and parent bone.

Working through naming hip/knee/ankle joints for the limb chain and deciding how points map to tip joints, then adding a decorative spike at the knee pointing outward, bound to that joint's bone. I'm also considering whether to connect the limb points with a sharp polyline versus a smooth catmull curve for the joint chain.

For the tail, I'm designing a spade-shaped blade at the tip using an extruded outline in the vertical plane, trying out different point coordinates to get a tapered, sharp-pointed shape that reads well in profile.

Then I'm sketching out the axe weapon: a wooden handle rod running diagonally across the left flank, attached near a spine joint, with a Leviathan-style axe head extruded near the top of the handle.

Adding ember particle effects scattered across the body, dorsal bone spikes along the spine, and broken spear props on the flank, then wiring up the chain hierarchy with the spine's last joint as the neck parent before finalizing the export.

Now I'm positioning the multi-head neck setup—placing five neck bases along the chest with mirrored left/right offsets, sizing the heads to taper from center outward, and plotting curved neck control points that lean back and arc upward into each head position.

I'm naming the head and jaw joints for rigging, deciding to pose the jaw rotation after assembling its parts, and planning the loft structure using station data (position, width, height) to shape the neck geometry and collar rings.

For the collar ring, I'll map points to their `.at` position but keep an explicit bone reference to the second neck joint so the rigid attachment stays correct even though the chain sweep inherits bone info by nearest joint otherwise. Time to write it all out.
